audits.dominantPattern: P9/P5 abstract noun or geography carrying physical behaviour
audits.secondSweepNotes: Every sentence was re-read for inanimate or abstract subjects carrying agency, cognition, combustion or physical-behaviour verbs, for actors demoted into instrument phrases, and for body-part subjects. The crystal and staff verbs (ticked, woke, shifted all on its own), the drag, the cold and frost travelling up the ash, the wards holding and thinning, and the construct's 'one part to wait' are all in-world mechanics. They fall under the subject-matter defense, so they are documented as KEEPs. Brask's moving thumb (L74, L78, L98, L717, L827, L847) is an involuntary tell that Windrunner and Jaina read, so it falls under the Pattern 8 involuntary exception. The sweep found two kills: an abstract 'price' doing the physical travelling of the frost (L687) and the village 'wearing' a haze (L969).

findings.text: The price came up the staff after.
findings.subject: the price
findings.verb: came up (and, in the next sentence, 'It went into the left hand')
findings.realAgent: The frost backlash, the cold coming back up the ash. The chapter names it concretely everywhere else (L296, L587, L667).
findings.reason: Pattern 9. An abstraction ('price') carries the physical travel of the cold up the staff and into the hand, while the concrete agent, the cold, has been pushed out of subject position. The zone overlaps a telegram_run flagged by the texture scorer, around 'Her arm was ice from the fingers to the shoulder'.
findings.suggestedFix: The cold came up the staff after, the price of it.

findings.text: The bakehouse sent none, and the village lay under the morning without the brown haze it had worn when she rode in, smaller without it, and barer.
findings.subject: the village
findings.realAgent: The bakehouse smoke (L488 'its smoke brown and warm and lying along the lane'; L5 'Bread smoke lay over all of it'). The haze hung over the village. The village did nothing.
findings.reason: Geography is given a clothing verb ('worn'), which dresses the place up instead of saying where the haze was. The chapter has already set the haze up literally as smoke lying over the lane. 'The bakehouse sent none' is kept as a literal chimney-emission idiom, and only the 'worn' clause needs to change.
findings.suggestedFix: The bakehouse sent none, and the village lay under the morning without the brown haze that had hung over it when she rode in, smaller without it, and barer.
